cases.explain: «телячьего двора» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Where are the hurdles for the calves’ paddock?”

cases.sentence: Пока седлали лошадь, Левин опять подозвал вертевшегося на виду приказчика, чтобы помириться с ним, и стал говорить ему о предстоящих весенних работах и ___.
cases.explain: «хозяйственных планах» — after the preposition «о», for location or topic.
cases.translation: While they were saddling his horse, Levin again called up the bailiff, who was hanging about in sight, to make it up with him, and began talking to him about the spring operations before them, and his plans for the farm.

cases.sentence: Возку навоза начать раньше, чтобы до ___ все было кончено.
cases.explain: «раннего покоса» — after the preposition «до», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: The wagons were to begin carting manure earlier, so as to get all done before the early mowing. And the ploughing of the further land to go on without a break so as to let it ripen lying fallow. And the mowing to be all done by hired labor, not on half-profits. The bailiff listened attentively, and obviously made an effort to approve of his employer’s projects. But still he had that look Levin knew so well that always irritated him, a look of hopelessness and despondency. That look said: “That’s all very well, but as God wills.”

cases.sentence: – Слушаю-с, – ответил Василий и взялся за голову лошади. – А уж сев, Константин Дмитрич, – сказал он, заискивая, – ___.
cases.explain: «первый сорт» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Yes, sir,” answered Vassily, and he took the horse’s head. “What a sowing, Konstantin Dmitrievitch,” he said, hesitating; “first rate. Only it’s a work to get about! You drag a ton of earth on your shoes.”

cases.sentence: Левин сел на лошадь и поехал на поле, где был ___, и на то, которое плугом было приготовлено под яровую пшеницу.
cases.explain: «прошлогодний клевер» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Levin got on his horse and rode towards the field where was last year’s clover, and the one which was ploughed ready for the spring corn.

cases.sentence: Он уж весь отжил и твердо зеленел из-за посломанных ___ пшеницы.
cases.explain: «прошлогодних стеблей» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: The crop of clover coming up in the stubble was magnificent. It had survived everything, and stood up vividly green through the broken stalks of last year’s wheat. The horse sank in up to the pasterns, and he drew each hoof with a sucking sound out of the half-thawed ground. Over the ploughland riding was utterly impossible; the horse could only keep a foothold where there was ice, and in the thawing furrows he sank deep in at each step. The ploughland was in splendid condition; in a couple of days it would be fit for harrowing and sowing. Everything was capital, everything was cheering. Levin rode back across the streams, hoping the water would have gone down. And he did in fact get across, and startled two ducks. “There must be snipe too,” he thought, and just as he reached the turning homewards he met the forest keeper, who confirmed his theory about the snipe.
